title: High-Field Terahertz Spin Resonance in Cr$_2$O$_3$ above the Spin-Flop Transition
authors: Kaiyang Huang, Yuto Kinoshita, Natsuki Kanda, Takuya Matsuda, Masashi Tokunaga, Ryusuke Matsunaga, Yasuhiro H. Matsuda
abstract: We report single-shot terahertz time-domain spectroscopy of Cr$_2$O$_3$ in pulsed magnetic fields up to 30 T. Well above the spin-flop field, in the 20-30 T range, the resonance frequency exhibits a nearly linear field dependence with a slope of ~22 GHz/T, smaller than the 28 GHz/T reported from low-field measurements. This reduction is insensitive to temperature and to a 15° field tilt, suggesting an intrinsic high-field property.
summary: This work uses terahertz time-domain spectroscopy to measure spin resonance in $	ext{Cr}_2	ext{O}_3$ under very high magnetic fields. The key finding is that the resonance frequency's field dependence changes significantly above the spin-flop transition. This reduction in the slope is interpreted as evidence of magnetoelastic renormalization effects within the antiferromagnetic material.
main_problem: The study investigates the terahertz spin resonance behavior in the antiferromagnet $	ext{Cr}_2	ext{O}_3$ specifically in the high-field regime, well above the spin-flop transition.
main_result: The resonance frequency exhibits a nearly linear field dependence with a slope of $\sim 22 	ext{ GHz/T}$ in the $20-30 	ext{ T}$ range, which is significantly smaller than the slope measured at lower fields ($\sim 28 	ext{ GHz/T}$).
method: Single-shot terahertz time-domain spectroscopy ($	ext{THz-TDS}$) was employed using pulsed magnetic fields up to $30 	ext{ T}$ to probe the magnetic excitations.
model_or_system: The system is $	ext{Cr}_2	ext{O}_3$, an antiferromagnetic material. The analysis involves comparing the measured $\omega-H$ relation to theoretical models for quasi-ferromagnetic resonance ($	ext{QFMR}$) above the spin-flop transition.
key_observables: Resonance frequency ($\omega$) as a function of applied magnetic field ($H$) and temperature ($T$).
important_parameters: High magnetic field regime ($20-30 	ext{ T}$), spin-flop field ($\approx 6 	ext{ T}$), and the derived effective anisotropy parameter ($b$).
main_assumptions: The reduction in the high-field slope is attributed to magnetoelastic renormalization of the anisotropy within the spin-flop phase.
figures_summary: Figure 1 presents $	ext{THz}$ time-domain waveforms, differential signals, resonance spectra, and the derived $\omega-H$ relationship, including a linear fit for the high-field regime.
paper_structure: The paper presents experimental measurements using $	ext{THz-TDS}$ on $	ext{Cr}_2	ext{O}_3$, analyzes the resonance frequency dependence on the magnetic field across different regimes (low-field vs. high-field), and compares the observed high-field slope to theoretical predictions incorporating magnetoelastic effects.
why_interesting: The observation of a field-dependent renormalization of the magnetic resonance frequency, quantified by the slope reduction, provides insight into the coupling between magnetic order and lattice strain in quantum magnets.
